proof_summary: Writing the target as \(4n(n+1)+1\) reduces the problem to an XOR of consecutive quadratic products; a greedy bit lift, using \(g(m+2^s)\equiv g(m)+2^s\pmod{2^{s+1}}\), constructs \(M<2^{n+1}\) with \(g(M)\equiv n(n+1)\pmod{2^{n+1}}\). According as adding \(M\) to \(M^2\bmod 2^{n+1}\) creates a carry, one takes the even candidate built from \(M\) or the odd candidate built from its complement \(2^{n+1}-M\); in either case the two XOR inputs have equal high parts, so the XOR is below the modulus and the modular equality becomes exact.
